extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, assignees, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures governing public and authorized access to U.S. patent application files (provisional, nonprovisional, reissue, reexamination, international) including when files are confidential, when copies may be furnished, powers to inspect, petitions for access, FOIA handling, and related special circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of patent application information (37 CFR 1.14(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that have not been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) are generally preserved in confidence pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(a). Information concerning filing, pendency, subject matter, status, and access will only be given to the public as set forth in § 1.11 or in § 1.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the default rule of confidentiality for unpublished applications and frames all exceptions in the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of unpublished abandoned applications identified or relied upon (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The file contents of an unpublished, abandoned application may be made available to the public if the application is identified in a U.S. patent, statutory invention registration, U.S. patent application publication, or an international application publication published under PCT Article 21(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application is considered identified when application/serial number and filing date, first named inventor, title, and filing date or other application-specific information are provided in the text of the patent (not merely in file contents). Copies of the application-as-filed or specific documents may be provided upon written request and payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of copies where benefit is claimed in an issued or published document (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the file contents of an unpublished pending application may be provided to any person upon written request and payment of fee if the benefit of the application is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365 in an application or patent that has issued or published as described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies provided may include application-as-filed or specific documents in the file; the Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application except as provided in paragraphs (c) or (h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability when application is incorporated by reference or otherwise identified (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the application as originally filed of an unpublished pending application may be provided upon written request and payment of fee if the application is incorporated by reference or otherwise identified in a U.S. patent, statutory invention registration, U.S. patent application publication, or international application publication under PCT Article 21(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Again, written request and fee are required; paper file access is restricted as noted above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office permits applicant access to prior pending application relied upon for filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a patent relies on the filing date of an earlier but still pending application, the Office permits an applicant to obtain a copy of the prior application (as originally filed or pending file history) upon written request to the Office of Public Records and payment of appropriate fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This facilitates verification of priority claims; availability also ties into the public availability rules after publication of certain documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to provisional applications limited to authorized parties
rubrics_metrics.description: In provisional applications, access or certified copies will only be given to parties with written authority from a named inventor, the assignee of record, or the attorney or agent of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications may lack an oath/declaration and power of attorney; certified copies requested by the registered attorney/agent named in the provisional will be supplied to the correspondence address. Provisional applications may also be available under §1.14(a)(1)(iv) if relied upon and identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board handles petitions for access in interferences (37 CFR 1.612)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences handles all petitions for access to applications involved in an interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.612 for procedures specific to interference files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive publications make entire application public
rubrics_metrics.description: If a defensive publication has been published, the entire application is available to the public for inspection and obtaining copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 711.06 for details on defensive publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application public inspection rules (37 CFR 1.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.11(b) opens reissue applications filed after March 1, 1977 to inspection by the general public and provides for announcement of filings in the Official Gazette (except for certain continued prosecution applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: announcement in Official Gazette; TC-supervised inspection; no access while application is actively processed; files released for publication are not available until patent issues; requests for copies directed to Mail Stop Document Services; copies priced per 37 CFR 1.19(b)(1). Older reissue applications may be subject to petitions for access handled liberally by Special Program Examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination file availability and format
rubrics_metrics.description: An announcement of filing each request for reexamination (with fee paid) and each reexamination ordered by the Director will be published in the Official Gazette. A reexamination file is normally not open until scanned into the CRU reexamination database, at which point an electronic copy is made available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: REPS terminal available in Patent Search Room; access is free; copies are 25 cents per page. All reexamination files are available to the public in electronic format only. See MPEP § 2232.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Director/Board decisions with precedential value (37 CFR 1.14(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions by the Director or the Board that would not otherwise be open to public inspection may be published or made available if the Director believes the decision involves an interpretation of patent laws/regulations of precedential value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant or party must be given notice and opportunity to object in writing within two months on grounds that the decision discloses trade secret/confidential info; objections must identify deletions needed or explain withholding; party given at least twenty days to request reconsideration and seek court review before portions are made public over objection. Office anticipates publishing only a few dozen such decisions per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA request requirements for USPTO records (37 CFR 102.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for USPTO records not customarily made available must be in writing and will be processed under FOIA regardless of whether FOIA is mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be sent to the USPTO FOIA Officer; mark envelope for quickest handling. For records about oneself or another individual, additional requirements (authorization or proof of death) apply. Requests must describe records with enough detail to enable location; the FOIA Officer will inform requester if the description is insufficient and may discuss modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to inspect requirements (37 CFR 1.14(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to a pending or abandoned application may be provided to any person if the application file is available and contains written authority (power to inspect) signed by an applicant, an attorney or agent of record, an authorized official of an assignee of record, or a registered attorney/agent named in accompanying papers when no oath/declaration has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an executed oath/declaration has been filed, only the applicant (one of joint applicants), an attorney/agent of record (if power of attorney filed), or an assignee of record may access the pending application unless written authority from one of those parties is made of record or upon written order of the Director. A person acting in representative capacity may execute power to inspect only under specified conditions. Approval by primary examiner not required; technical support staff verifies signature and enters power into file; unacceptable powers prompt notification of nonentry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of oath/declaration on previously filed powers to inspect
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an executed oath or declaration pursuant to 37 CFR 1.63 or 1.497 has been filed, any previously filed power to inspect signed by a registered attorney or agent who does not have a power of attorney will cease to have effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 402 for discussion of power of attorney implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFW applications and PAIR access; powers to inspect not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Powers to inspect are not accepted in Image File Wrapper (IFW) applications. IFW applications are available through Private PAIR (or Public PAIR for published applications/patents); pro se applicants and attorneys of record have direct access through Private PAIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant/assignee/attorney cannot view an IFW application through PAIR, a copy must be purchased from the Office of Public Records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers to inspect as continuing until rescinded (applicant/attorney/assignee)
rubrics_metrics.description: An unrestricted power to inspect given by an applicant, attorney/agent of record, or assignee is recognized as in effect until rescinded so long as the signer retains connection with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission granted by the Director is not necessarily continuing because conditions justifying it may change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access on oral request and identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Access will be given on oral request to any applicant, patentee, assignee, or attorney/agent of record only upon proof of identity or recognition based on personal acquaintance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For powers of attorney/authorizations given to registered firms prior to July 2, 1971, access will be given to registered members/employees with signatory power. Unregistered employees and others not covered require written authorization (power to inspect) signed by an authorized person; the authorization must specifically name the person and identify the application number and be limited to a single application. Form PTO/SB/67 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application access and certified copy handling for non-named requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: In provisional applications, access or certified copies may only be requested by parties with written authority from a named inventor, assignee of record, or attorney/agent of record unless the application is available under specific public-access provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester is not a named inventor/assignee/attorney, the certified copy will be supplied to the correspondence address of the provisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspended or excluded practitioners cannot inspect
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO employees are forbidden to hold oral or written communication with an attorney or agent suspended or excluded from practice regarding an application unless that attorney/agent is the applicant. Power to inspect given to such attorney/agent will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects the Office and applicants from unauthorized representation by disbarred/suspended practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee control of inspection and inventor access
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignee of record of the entire interest in an application may intervene in prosecution and appoint an attorney of choice; such intervention does not automatically exclude the applicant from access unless the assignee files a separate request to prevent inventor access and the request is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to prevent inventor access should be filed as a separate paper under 37 CFR 1.4(c) directed to Office of Petitions; if granted the inventor will be informed and will only be permitted inspection upon sufficient showing why inspection is necessary to conserve rights (with case citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of assignee of part interest or exclusive licensee to inspect
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee of a part interest or a licensee of exclusive right is entitled to inspect the application, even though only the assignee of the entire interest can intervene to exclude the applicant from prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 402.10 for applications accorded status under 37 CFR 1.47.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of international applications (PCT Article 30) prior to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau and International Searching Authorities shall not allow access by any person or authority to the international application before international publication unless requested or authorized by the applicant; national Offices shall not allow access before the earliest of international publication, receipt under Article 20, or receipt under Article 22, except as authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Offices may publish only limited identifying data (receiving Office, applicant name, international filing date, international application number, title). Exceptions include transmittals to ISAs, Article 13 transmittals, communications under Article 20, and judicial authority purposes. 'Access' covers any means third parties may acquire cognizance, and publication generally cannot occur before 20 months from priority date if international publication has not taken place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of international preliminary examination (PCT Article 38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the International Bureau nor the International Preliminary Examining Authority shall, unless requested/authorized by the applicant, allow access to the file of the international preliminary examination, except to elected Offices once the international preliminary examination report has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to Articles 36 and 37 provisions; authorities should not give information on issuance/non-issuance of reports or on withdrawal/non-withdrawal of demands/elections unless authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 368 restrictions on disclosure of international applications kept secret
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application is ordered to be kept secret or a license to file in a foreign country is refused, the PTO when acting in PCT capacities may not disclose the contents of such application to anyone not authorized to receive such disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows treaty obligations; international filing in another country considered filing in a foreign country under chapter 17 rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for furnishing copies of international application files (37 CFR 1.14(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of international application files for international applications that designate the U.S. and have been published under PCT Article 21(2), or copies of a document in such files, will be furnished upon written request showing publication and U.S. designation and payment of appropriate fee, if (i) Home Copy filed with U.S. Receiving Office, (ii) Search Copy where U.S. acted as ISA (except written opinion unavailable until 30 months), or (iii) Examination Copy where U.S. acted as IPEA and IPER has issued and U.S. was elected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English language translation copies may be furnished upon similar showing and fee. Copies of application-as-filed will not be provided prior to international publication. Access to Examination Copy under certain paragraphs is limited per PCT Articles and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions for access under special circumstances (37 CFR 1.14(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office, sua sponte or on petition, may provide access or copies of all or part of an application if necessary to carry out an Act of Congress or warranted by other special circumstances. A petition must include the fee set forth in § 1.17(h) and a showing that access is necessary to carry out an Act of Congress or that special circumstances exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition should include full post office address, telephone and facsimile to expedite handling; may be filed with proof of service on applicant/assignee/attorney or filed in duplicate for Office to send duplicate to applicant. Separate petition and fee required for each application. Petition must show why access desired and why petitioner believes entitled. Applicant normally given limited period (e.g., ~3 weeks) to state objection; if applicant has no objection access granted; if objection raised or no response, petition decided on record. If access is granted, applicant objections become available to petitioner; if denied petitioner will not receive copies of applicant objections. 'Special circumstances' examples include where applicant used application to interfere with competitor's business or customers; obtaining power to inspect from assignee/inventor may be more expeditious.
